method: A word table and one copying rule, fitted on the public training pages only; no glyph, word or position is named. Line lengths are drawn from the public paragraph line lengths (5 to 14 words). Each word is drawn independently from the public word list by frequency, except that with probability 0.025 the writer instead looks at the line directly above, picks one of its words of four or more glyphs at random, and writes a word from the public word list that differs from it by exactly one glyph (one inserted, dropped or replaced); if the list holds no such word it draws by frequency as usual. Lines holding a four-word run of the manuscript are redrawn. This is Timm's self-citation reduced to its smallest form, and it does write the target pattern in directly (a copy from the line above with one glyph changed), so by the red team's own rule it should count as a weak refutation if a second look says so: what it shows is how little copying the fact needs, not that the copying arises from something else. Fitting, all on the practice split: the measured excess grows about in proportion to the copying rate. At 0.04 three seeds gave 0.029, 0.053, 0.052 (two over the fact's upper bound of 0.045); at 0.08 and 0.12 one seed each gave 0.088 and 0.117 (over); at 0.025 four seeds gave 0.021, 0.040, 0.022 (pass) and 0.008 (under the floor of 0.012). This text is seed 1 at 0.025, the first seed drawn, not the best of the four. The spread between seeds is as wide as the fact's window, so a miss on the hidden pages would be sampling noise as easily as a failure of the procedure; the fact's own notes report the same spread for the manuscript.
